problem.label: WHY IT MATTERS
problem.headline: Solo-dining spaces have solvable problems

claims.claim: Solo-dining discomfort is a design problem, not a personal one.
claims.evidence: Both Korean and international diners ranked social pressure from others as their top discomfort (26–28%). A single partition can structurally eliminate this anxiety.

claims.claim: Eating alone more often doesn't make it more comfortable. The space has to change.
claims.evidence: International students — who eat alone more frequently than Koreans — actually reported higher discomfort (International 2.7 / Korean 2.3 out of 5). Frequency is not the solution.

claims.claim: Korean and international diners face completely different barriers in the same space.
claims.evidence: The share citing language barriers as a pain point: Korean 0%, International 16%. The same restaurant creates entirely different entry experiences for each group.

claims.claim: Remove even one barrier, and customers who haven't arrived yet will start coming.
claims.evidence: Our Service Safari found three things missing: an English kiosk, dietary labels, and wayfinding. This space was effectively closed to international customers.
claims.source: Table One Service Safari, Misung Katsu Chuncheon, 2026

problem.closing: The economic barriers are low. The CX barriers are high. Fix them, and customers ready to spend are waiting.

services.label: SERVICES
services.headline: 3 Service Packages
services.sub: We solve research-identified problems with research-validated solutions.

items.name: Space Redesign
items.summary: We redesign partition layouts and seating structure so solo diners can choose their seat on their own terms.
items.detail: When solo diners are directed to single seats, the sense of exclusion is a space design problem, not a service issue. Installing partitions converts 4-seat tables into solo-friendly zones. When there's a choice, there's dignity.
deliverables: On-site space audit and customer flow analysis
Solo zone design and signage system
items.painSolved: Loss of seat autonomy / Forced single-seat assignment / Awkward table layout
items.curbCut: Separated seating designed for solo diners also enhances privacy for couples and group diners.

items.name: Kiosk Integration
items.summary: Guests self-select their seat on arrival, and the choice reflects instantly on the owner's screen in the kitchen.
items.detail: This solves two simultaneous problems: the owner can't leave the kitchen to greet guests, and guests don't know where to sit. Guests see the full seat map and choose independently. The owner stays informed in real time without stepping out. It connects the line of internal interaction through a digital bridge.
deliverables: Guest kiosk UI design and delivery
Korean, English, and Arabic multilingual support
items.painSolved: No seating guidance / Language barriers / Contactless preference / Owner greeting burden
items.curbCut: The English-language UI built for international guests also aligns with Korean guests' preference for contactless ordering.

items.name: Owner Onboarding
items.summary: We provide staff communication guides, Solo-Friendly Certification, and a manual for serving international guests.
items.detail: Space and technology change, but the experience doesn't unless people do too. The words an owner says to a solo diner set the tone for the entire CX. Our communication guide starts from expressions real users said they wanted, drawn directly from our research.
deliverables: Basic international guest response cards (English and Arabic)
Table One platform registration and listing
items.painSolved: Unfriendly staff responses / Fear of international guest communication / Perceived discrimination against solo diners
items.curbCut: The international guest communication manual eliminates the owner's anxiety about serving foreign customers and opens a new revenue stream.

effects.label: WHY IT WORKS
effects.headline: Business Impact
effects.sub: Change the space, change the experience. Change the experience, change the revenue.

items.title: International Customer Acquisition
items.desc: An English-language kiosk and dietary labels open the door to international students who previously couldn't access the restaurant. Hallym University alone has over 1,200 international students enrolled.

items.title: Improved Table Turnover
items.desc: Partition-based seating resolves the problem of solo diners occupying 4-seat tables for extended periods, improving seat utilization during peak hours.
items.source: Table One Space Redesign Pilot Analysis

items.title: Higher Return Visit Rate
items.desc: Solo diners who feel respected come back. Our research confirmed that feeling disrespected in a dining environment reduces return visit intent.

items.title: Multilingual Accessibility
items.desc: We convert a Korean-only environment into a multilingual one, removing the ordering anxiety and language stress that international customers face.

portfolio.label: CASE STUDY
portfolio.headline: Case Study
portfolio.sub: From research to solution design, verified in the field.

cases.challenge: Solo diners funneled to single seats, Korean-only kiosk, triple entry barriers for international customers
approach: Service Safari direct experience (international student persona)
Survey n=64 + In-Depth Interviews (IDI) n=4, cross-validated
Two Customer Journey Maps created (Korean vs. international comparison)
Service Blueprint designed (kiosk line of internal interaction included)
solutions: Partition layout plan, 1-person/4-person convertible seating design
Seat selection kiosk UI design (Korean + English)
cases.keyInsight: The economic barriers are low. The CX barriers are high. Three missing elements were costing real revenue.
before: No dietary information for international guests
